knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A hollow tile is lifted, checked and re-bedded before grouting. Grouting over it hides the fault and leaves the tile to crack under load.
Acid-based cleaners can mark or etch natural stone and unglazed tile unless the data sheet allows them. The other options are not the cleaner the question asks about.
The sample lift is taken while the bed is still open, so a poor coverage or level can be corrected by lifting and re-setting.
Water is added to grout only where the data sheet allows it. Otherwise the batch is discarded and a fresh one is mixed within the working time.

practicalCriteria: Sets one full row of tiles on a simulated area with spacers, and the joint width is consistent across the row on assessor inspection.
Checks each tile's level against its neighbour with a straight edge, and corrects at least one proud tile by lifting and re-setting it while the adhesive is workable.
Takes one sample lift, photographs the back of the tile, and records the coverage against the requirement written in the task sheet.
Finds a simulated hollow tile by sound, re-beds it, and records the fix before any grouting in that area.
Grouts a sample panel with diagonal strokes, cleans the haze with a damp sponge and clean water, and the assessor finds no voids in the joints after cure.
passRule: All five practical criteria met on the sample, with the records complete. Observed by an assessor. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Setting and coverage check record, with the sample lift photograph
Adhesive and grout product record with the data sheet reference
stopWorkCriteria: A hollow tile is grouted over
An acid-based cleaner is used on natural stone or unglazed tile without data sheet approval
Grouting continues without checking adhesive coverage
